transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees (as listed): Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Aperture), Jules Rivera (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (Product), Marco Li (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, optional):
Aperture is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for a payments fraud-detection POC. Primary criteria: p95 latency <150ms for short-text classification, cost per 1M tokens target, audit logs/KMS compliance, and throughput of 400 concurrent requests. Customer wants a 4-week POC with a 48h high-load benchmark in week 3.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Park: okay great everyone thanks for joining, um, let's do quick intros then we'll jump into the scoping goals, this is Lena from Redwood, AE on this account.
[00:12] Marcus Chen: Marcus here, I'm the SE - I'll run the bench plan and help with infra hooks.
[00:16] Samir Patel: Samir, CTO at Aperture Financial. Really appreciate you all. We've got Jules, Priya, Marco on.
[00:24] Jules Rivera: hey all.
[00:26] Priya Singh: hi.
[00:28] Marco Li: Marco here, security.
[00:30] Lena Park: cool, high level today we want to align on success metrics, expected workload (qps and token distribution), what benchmarks look like, and how we decide between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for the POC. Also call out compliance asks.

[00:45] Samir Patel: right, so quick context - we run real-time fraud scoring on payment streams, per-call prompt is ~30-80 tokens, average 45, but we also have batch enrichment jobs that hit the model with longer context like 512 tokens occasionally. Latency matters: customer-facing decisions need <200ms ideally, p95 target is 150ms. Throughput: peak ~400 req/s during batch windows, baseline 80-120 req/s. Cost is also a major gate - we have internal budgets.

[01:20] Marcus Chen: gotcha. So two main workload modes - interactive short prompts and periodic heavy batch. For short prompts we can prioritize low-latency knobs: smaller model variants, aggressive KV/prefix caching, lower batching windows. For batch we can use larger instance pools and allow higher tail latency.

[01:50] Jules Rivera: question: for Dedicated vs Hosted, how much control will we have over GPU types and autoscale? Our infra runs in AWS us-east and we want to avoid cross-region egress.
[02:05] Lena Park: Hosted can be region pinned to us-east, but it's multi-tenant; Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with specific instance types and predictable throughput; Private is full VPC/on-prem with customer-managed infra. Autoscale for Dedicated is configurable - you set policies and burst capacity, we'd recommend Dedicated for sustained high throughput and tight latency SLOs.

[02:35] Priya Singh: on the compliance side, Marco will lead, but we need SOC 2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. Private would be simplest for data residency but more ops. Is KMS available for Hosted?
[02:50] Marcus Chen: Hosted offers envelope encryption and integration with common KMS providers, but keys are managed by Redwood unless you pick Dedicated with customer KMS or Private where you manage keys.

[03:10] Marco Li: we also need immutable audit logs for 12 months, plus retention policy.
[03:16] Lena Park: that's supported in Dedicated and Private as an add-on for Hosted; we can include audit export to your S3 with log signing. We'll note that in the POC checklist.

[03:30] [Speaker 5]: uh hmm..
[03:33] Samir Patel: what's typical POC length you recommend? We were thinking 4 weeks.
[03:38] Marcus Chen: 4 weeks is what we do a lot - week 0/1 baseline and deploy, week 2 optimization and tuning (caching, batching, quantize model), week 3 heavy benchmark run 48 hours, week 4 analysis and decision.

[03:55] Lena Park: success criteria we should define now - proposed: p95 latency under 150ms for short prompts on Dedicated; throughput sustaining 350-400 req/s with acceptable cost; model accuracy parity within 2% of your baseline classifier; and security checklist passed (SOC2 items, KMS). Thoughts?

[04:18] Priya Singh: accuracy parity is key - can't regress. We will provide labeled sample set for regression tests.
[04:24] Samir Patel: cost target? can you ballpark for the baseline workloads?
[04:29] Marcus Chen: rough numbers: hosted lowest setup friction but per-token unit cost slightly higher; Dedicated amortizes to lower per-token at scale. For your mix (50% short, 50% batch by compute), I'd estimate per-month run cost during bench ~ $Xk for Dedicated baseline vs $Yk for Hosted — we'll send a specific pricing sheet. Quantization and batching will reduce cost notably.
[04:55] Lena Park: note those are estimates; the POC will run cost modeling with actual token counts you provide.
[05:05] Jules Rivera: network: for Private we want on-prem air-gapped option as a fallback. Is Redwood's Private stack supported on bare-metal?
[05:14] Marcus Chen: yes, Private can be on-prem; there are packaging options and we do a preflight checklist. It takes more lead time — typically 6-10 weeks to onboard for Private, whereas Dedicated is 1-2 weeks if capacity is available. Hosted is immediate.
[05:32] Samir Patel: timeline impact is huge for us; if we need a quick POC in 4 weeks we probably can't do Private. Might be Dedicated or Hosted.

[05:45] Lena Park: exactly, that's the decision axis: speed to value vs control vs unit cost vs compliance. We'll map it out in a decision matrix.

[06:00] [01:10] Marcus Chen: on benchmarks: we'll run two modes - synthetic replay that mimics your 48h traffic and a golden-run with real payloads if you can provide them. Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, and error rates. Also do end-to-end request tracing for tail latency sources.
[06:30] Priya Singh: can you show us what the benchmark script looks like? We want to ensure it doesn't bias towards caching we wouldn't get in production.
[06:40] Marcus Chen: yep, script has options: cold-cache runs, warm-cache runs, variable prefix distribution. We'll include randomization seeds and can run a cold-start sweep.
[06:52] Jules Rivera: how do you handle fallbacks in case of capacity or model failure? We want graceful degradation - send to smaller model or queued responses?
[07:02] Lena Park: Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants; also capacity tiers so you can set a canary and fallback routes. We'll show your team the console runbook.
[07:18] Samir Patel: regarding data retention during bench, we need logs masked and PII redaction, is that doable?
[07:25] Marcus Chen: we offer masking hooks and deterministic hashing at the request layer; we can also run on customer-provided VPC for Private/Dedicated to keep logs in your account.
[07:38] Marco Li: encryption-at-rest and in-transit ok? HSM options?
[07:42] Lena Park: yes, TLS in transit, KMS for keys; Dedicated supports using your KMS keys and HSM integrations as an enterprise add-on.
[07:52] [08:10] Speaker 5: mmm
[08:12] Marcus Chen: let's lock on specific success metrics to include in the POC doc: numerical items we can measure. Proposed list: (1) p95 <150ms for short prompts on production-like traffic, (2) 99.9% availability for the benchmark window, (3) less than 2% model quality regression on your labeled set, (4) cost per 1M tokens under target (we'll populate target after we get your token counts), (5) security signoffs (SOC2 checklist items completed).
[08:48] Priya Singh: that looks reasonable. I'll add data residency and SSO success as gating items.
[08:55] Samir Patel: ok good. What does the POC environment look like for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[09:02] Marcus Chen: Hosted: quick API keys, region pinning, limited KMS; good for immediate testing. Dedicated: we provision reserved pool in us-east, you get predictable baseline throughput with options to choose instance types; Private: we deliver control plane on your VPC or on-prem package and you own the infra. For the POC we recommend Dedicated if you want realistic performance and cost estimates without the ops of Private.
[09:32] Lena Park: and for quick proof of concept, we often do a two-path approach: spin up Hosted to validate functional and quality aspects in ~3 days, parallel provision Dedicated sandbox for performance runs in week 1-2. That shortens the decision cycle.
[09:48] Jules Rivera: layering both sounds good. Are there any hidden limits on concurrent requests or tokenizer differences? We've seen tokenization mismatch cause issues with other vendors.
[09:59] Marcus Chen: we use standard tokenizers and include tokenizer debug dumps. We'll provide a tokenization diff report. Also note quantization can slightly change numeric outputs so we'll include a regression checker.
[10:18] Samir Patel: benchmark schedule - can Redwood drive the 48h bench or we provide a hold window?
[10:24] Marcus Chen: Redwood can drive with SE on call; we'll need your VPC/test creds and a 2-hour maintenance window scheduled with your infra for the big runs.
[10:34] Priya Singh: let's talk numbers: for the 48h run what GPU counts are you expecting to allocate for Dedicated?
[10:40] Marcus Chen: ballpark for your mix maybe 4x A100 equivalents for sustained 400 qps on model phi-small (example), but depending on model variant and sequence length this could change; we'll provide a sizing doc.
[10:55] Lena Park: we'll include a spreadsheet with a few scenarios: optimistic (more quantization, aggressive caching), realistic (baseline), and conservative (worst-case).
[11:05] Jules Rivera: lead time for Dedicated capacity? If we sign up now, how fast?
[11:10] Lena Park: typically 1-2 weeks to provision reserved pool if capacity is available; we'll check current availability in us-east and confirm.
[11:18] Marco Li: private on-prem timeline again? You said 6-10 weeks. Too long for our Q3 milestones.
[11:24] Samir Patel: yes, Q3 deliverable so Private probably not viable for this cycle unless critical.
[11:30] Marcus Chen: understood.
[11:32] [11:40] Lena Park: ok let's surface a decision matrix real quick - speed: Hosted fastest, Dedicated medium, Private slow; control: Private>Dedicated>Hosted; unit cost: Private/Dedicated lower at scale vs Hosted; compliance: Private/Dedicated stronger. We'll put this in the doc.
[11:55] Samir Patel: anything else we need to finalize now?
[11:58] Priya Singh: we need the POC doc, pricing, and benchmark plan. Also a security questionnaire — Marco will share our internal questionnaire.
[12:06] Marcus Chen: action items covered. We'll include a proposed bench date 2025-07-15 pending your VPC creds.
[12:12] Lena Park: recap and next steps: Lena to send POC template + pricing by 7/10; Marcus will deliver benchmark scripts and sizing doc by 7/14; Aperture to provide sample prompts + 48h traffic profile by 7/11; Marco to send security questionnaire by 7/11. We'll schedule the 48h benchmark window for 7/15 subject to infra approvals.
[12:36] Samir Patel: sounds good. Appreciate the clarity.
[12:40] Lena Park: cool thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and drop the materials into the shared folder.
[12:46] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some speaker labels may be generic (Speaker 5). Occasional ASR errors: "K V cache" vs "KV cache", "A100" sometimes transcribed as "A one hundred".
